title: Post from @PortAlderMom_Kris: "High School INSPECTED = SAFE"

fields.avatarBrief: woman in her late thirties in a rain jacket, smiling selfie on the Port Alder waterfront with two young kids
fields.text: GOOD NEWS: the county stamped the high school INSPECTED = SAFE. Engineers say it can't fall down so bring your whole family and the dogs, it's the safest building in the county now even if there's another big one 🙏 #PortAlderStrong #Tsunami
fields.attachedImageBrief: rain-streaked phone photo of a green ATC-20 'INSPECTED' placard taped to the glass entry door of the Marlow Coast High School gym, the time 13:10 and an inspector's name handwritten in marker, wet people in hoodies crowded behind the glass

comments.author: Dev P.
comments.text: So the Front Street shops with green tags are safe to reopen too?? My store is on Front, can I go open up and get the stock out?

comments.author: Lori M.
comments.text: Don't come up here with the dogs, we're AT the high school. Gym is full, they're not letting anyone else in, maybe 60 of us standing outside the door in the rain. And the lights and heat just went out.

comments.author: Marcus T.
comments.text: My cousin volunteers with the Red Cross. She says they have cots and blankets sitting in Salem but no truck can get here, 101 and 6 are both closed.

instructorNote: Misinformation inject: put the post on screen, then read out the shelter lead's call (400 registered, which is the limit; 60 people at the door; generator died at 13:14 and won't restart; reunification laptop at 20% battery) and the Red Cross email from 13:17 (500 cots and 1,000 blankets stuck in Salem until ODOT names a route or the Coast Guard does a sling load). Watch whether the PIO corrects the post on every working channel, saying a green placard means no apparent hazard at the time of inspection, gives no guarantee against aftershocks, and that Front Street hasn't been inspected. Also watch whether Command finds a generator tech, opens an overflow site such as the EOC area or the Station 3 bays, and requests cots through OEM and the Coast Guard, and whether Fire moves the 60 people at the door.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Rain-streaked smartphone snapshot taken from outside a high school gym's glass entry doors on a grey, stormy early afternoon. A bright green sheet of paper is taped at chest height to the wet glass, and its small handwritten marks are blurred and unreadable behind the water droplets. Behind the glass, a crowd of tired, soaked adults and children in hoodies and rain jackets presses close together, with some holding dogs on leashes and others holding blankets. The gym interior behind them is dim. Beads of water run down the glass, with reflections of overcast sky and wet concrete. The phone is slightly tilted and held close, with harsh flash glare on the glass, a cold blue-grey cast and an anxious, crowded mood.
